assessment: The incumbent provides reservations, telephone/in-person changes and staffed key collection; eleven groups obtained a weekly booking. It does not establish the target: needs are unmeasured, three access conflicts occurred, and administration averaged 127.5 minutes weekly. The concrete limiting observation is 68% reserved capacity alongside declined requests concentrated on Tuesday/Thursday evenings. This weakens an aggregate-capacity explanation but does not demonstrate usable spare capacity: acceptable alternatives and most equipment requirements are unknown. Four groups rehearsing elsewhere likewise cannot establish successful access under undocumented arrangements. Late or unattended sessions do not establish that their time could reliably be reassigned.

openings.claim: Inherited booking times and unrecorded compatibility requirements may leave a feasible allocation undiscovered; aggregate spare capacity alone cannot establish this.
openings.delta: Test whether unused time can meet actual needs while protecting every requested weekly minimum, rather than treating nominal vacancies as interchangeable.
openings.prediction: A schedule using declared acceptable windows, necessary equipment and durations can either meet the 90% needs target plus every required weekly minimum, or expose a specific time/equipment bottleneck despite overall vacancies.
openings.probe: Use short contact conversations to record weekly needs, acceptable windows, equipment and minimum useful duration. Construct a paper allocation within the two rooms and existing staffed hours, preserving both performances. Compare its achievable coverage with existing bookings; count a 60-minute entitlement separately from a longer rehearsal need. Make no booking changes during this feasibility probe.
assumptions: Contacts can accurately describe their groups' needs.
Feasibility is unknown; no group is assumed willing to accept shorter rehearsals or different times.

openings.claim: A desk-authoritative ledger with unique reservation references and explicit replacement confirmations may reduce contradictory access expectations.
openings.delta: Give each telephone or in-person change one traceable current reservation; mark the online copy with its synchronization time.
openings.prediction: Conflicts caused by stale or duplicate confirmations decline, while logging costs may offset any reduction in clarification work.
openings.probe: Pilot the ledger within existing bookings and staffed hours; read back room, date, time and superseded reference on each change. Record conflict causes and all administration minutes for eight weeks, testing fewer than two conflicts and a weekly average at most 120 minutes.
assumptions: The desk and volunteer consistently consult the same ledger.
Two double-expectation incidents have unknown causes, so reconciliation may not prevent them.
